  Quant Experts: Token-aware Adaptive Error Reconstruction with Mixture of
          Experts for Large Vision-Language Models Quantization

      Chenwei Jia* Baoting Li* Xuchong Zhang† Mingzhuo Wei Bochen Lin Hongbin Sun
              State Key Laboratory of Human-Machine Hybrid Augmented Intelligence
                           Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
                                      Xi’an Jiaotong University
                                                         jiacw@stu.xjtu.edu.cn

                           Abstract
                                                                                     Modality-aware
Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) has emerged as an ef-                               Token-aware
fective technique for alleviating the substantial computa-                                                  e.g. SmoothQuant (Channel-wise static quantization)
tional and memory overheads of Vision-Language Models
                                                                                                                      Different modalities
(VLMs) by compressing both weights and activations with-
out retraining the full model. Existing PTQ methods pri-                             Modality-aware

marily rely on static identification and global compensa-                            Token-aware
tion of sensitive or outlier channels, yet they often overlook                                                    e.g. MBQ (Modality-aware quantization)
the distributional differences of these important channels
                                                                                                                              Different tokens
across inputs, leading to unsatisfactory quantization. In
                                                                                     Modality-aware
this work, we observe that the distributions and occurrence
frequencies of important channels vary significantly both                            Token-aware
across modalities and among tokens, even within the same                                                    Quant Experts (Token-aware adaptive quantization)
modality. Accordingly, we propose Quant Experts (QE),
                                                                                Figure 1. Illustration of Different Quantization Granularities. D
a token-aware adaptive error compensation with mixture-                         is the calibration data, and Wq is the quantized weight matrix.
of-experts for VLMs quantization. QE divides the impor-                         SmoothQuant [44] employs channel-wise with fixed scaling co-
tant channels into token-independent and token-dependent                        efficients to achieve global quantization. MBQ [23] presents
groups. For the former, a shared expert is designed for most                    a modality-aware strategy that focuses on sensitivities in input
tokens to compensate for global quantization error using a                      modalities. In contrast, we propose a token-aware adaptive quan-
low-rank adapter. For the latter, routed experts including                      tization that considers both global and local error reconstruction.
multiple routed low-rank adapters are elaborated to com-
pensate for local quantization error related to specific to-
kens. Extensive experiments demonstrate that QE consis-                         sion and acceleration while preserving accuracy. Among
tently enhances task accuracy across various quantization                       existing approaches, Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) is
settings and model scales, ranging from 2B to 70B param-                        widely adopted for its efficiency and compatibility without
eters, while maintaining performance comparable to full-                        retraining the full model. However, low-bit quantization
precision models.                                                               inevitably introduces numerical perturbations that degrade
                                                                                performance, a problem that is especially pronounced in
                                                                                multimodal scenarios [13].
1. Introduction                                                                     Recent studies on large-scale model quantization reveal
                                                                                significant variation in channel value distributions and sen-
Model quantization has become a key technique for reduc-                        sitivities, where a small set of outlier or highly sensitive
ing the computational and memory costs of large-scale mul-                      channels plays a key role in preserving model expressive-
timodal models [19]. By mapping weights and activations                         ness and accuracy. To mitigate quantization errors aris-
to low-bit representations, it achieves substantial compres-                    ing from these important channels, numerous methods have

4.4. Overheads Analysis and Kernel Performance
                                                                                 5. Conclusion
The low-rank adapter introduces additional computation
and memory overhead from the lightweight auxiliary matri-                        In this work, we reveal a key observation that the dis-
ces L·A and L·B . Let s denote the sequence length, d hid-                       tributions and occurrence frequencies of important chan-
den size, r(≪ d) the rank, and Nr (≪ d) the routed experts                       nels vary significantly both across modalities and among
count. The complexity analysis of a single layer is provided                     tokens, even within the same modality. Building on this
in Tab. 7, with computation quantified in terms of floating-                     insight, we propose Quant Experts (QE), a token-aware
point operations (FLOPs) and memory overhead evaluated                           adaptive error compensation for VLMs quantization, that
by the total number of parameters. Notably, QE incurs only                       dynamically adapts to such variations. Specifically, QE
minimal additional computational and memory costs com-                           employs a shared expert to robustly reconstruct token-
pared to the original linear, yet enables the quantized model                    independent channels and routed experts to adaptively com-
to recover accuracy comparable to full precision.                                pensate token-dependent ones, with each expert imple-
    To assess hardware efficiency, we develop an analyti-                        mented as a low-rank adapter. Comprehensive evaluations
cal performance model following the FlightLLM [47] ac-                           on diverse VLMs show that QE consistently outperforms
celerator architecture. Prefill-stage kernel speedups of lin-                    globally static PTQ baselines across different quantization
ear layers are measured with sequence length 128 using                           configurations.
